name: Question 2
problem:
Consider the following differential equation.

$$
{y}^{″}-y=10{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

The general solution to this equation can be written as

$$
y(x)=A{e}^{-x}+B{e}^{x}+g(x),
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are constants. Which of the following could be the function $g(x)?$

*Hint: Use the variation of parameters method. You may also wish to make use of the following result (integration constants omitted):*

$$
\int {e}^{2x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{5}{e}^{2x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2\operatorname{cos}⁡x)
$$

Question 2

Consider the following differential equation. y″−y=10excos⁡x The general solution to this equation can be written as y(x)=Ae−x+Bex+g(x), where A and B are constants. Which of the following could be the function g(x)?

Hint: Use the variation of parameters method. You may also wish to make use of the following result (integration constants omitted): ∫e2xcos⁡xdx=15e2x(sin⁡x+2cos⁡x)

a
 ex(5sin⁡x−cos⁡x)
b
 ex(4sin⁡x−2cos⁡x)
c
 ex(4sin⁡x−3cos⁡x)
d
 ex(2sin⁡x−4cos⁡x)
e
 ex(5sin⁡x−2cos⁡x)
